note: Study analyzes the 10m-JPY exemption threshold introduced by the 2004 reform.
Estimated from the 2016 Economic Census for firms in the 8m to below-10m JPY sales region; paper notes TDB small-firm coverage can bias bunching downward.
Value-added share in the nationalized bunching region, used by the paper for its tax-windfall calculation.
Paper uses an 8% VAT rate for the Table 4 nationalized calculation.
Nationalized excess-buncher estimate. It measures distorted firm-location in the sales distribution, not the number of firms proven to reduce real output.
Estimated tax windfall (lost tax collection), not a real-resource or GDP loss.

Assumes all estimated excess bunchers came from the 10m-11m transition region and each lost 1.5m JPY of real sales. Paper explicitly warns this can overstate lost sales if some bunching is tax avoidance.
Uses observed missing mass and assumes 1.5m JPY lost sales per corresponding firm. This remains assumption-dependent and is not a formal lower bound on welfare/GDP loss.
